audience.notes: Same adapted fears as the pillar brief. Fear A: 'we miss a legal deadline or a document lapses while we are busy or travelling, and the marriage is not valid'. Fear B: 'we pay for a beautiful wedding that turns out not to be a legal marriage, or paperwork breaks down between celebrant, registry and an overseas venue'. Paying parent: whether the marriage is recognised and provable at home. PAA ('What happens to a marriage that is not registered?', 'What is the best proof of marriage?') maps directly onto fear B. Anti-persona: no 'quickest' or 'cheapest' framing.

payload.search_intent: Informational, precise. The searcher has a date or a document in hand and wants to know: does it expire, when, and what if plans change. Two sub-intents: domestic (NOIM, certificate) and destination (overseas licence, CNI, apostille).
payload.angle: Most wedding paperwork does not 'expire', but almost all of it runs on a clock. Correct the '18-month validity' myth in the first 60 words, then give one clear map of every time limit that matters at home and abroad, with a single 'what lasts how long' table. The how-to stays in the pillar.
spoke_rules: Cover only time limits, expiry and what happens when dates move. Do not repeat the pillar's how-to: lodging and witnessing the NOIM, shortening of time, eligibility, documents list, state registry table, the three overseas routes.

Link up to the pillar at least twice: once in the first 150 words and once in the NOIM H2. Descriptive anchors, e.g. 'our full guide to marriage licence requirements in Australia' and 'how to give your Notice of Intended Marriage'. Never the bare anchor 'marriage licence'.
Reuse facts already verified for the pillar, Greece and Italy articles; new facts come only from research batches running now.
serp_gaps_to_win: Head term unserved: Google shows an XML dataset, a tax forum, a parliamentary PDF and Philippine image results. Any clear page can rank.

Myth correction: celebrant pages say the NOIM is 'valid for 18 months' in three inconsistent ways. Our pillar's research says 18 months is the earliest you can give notice, not a validity period. Snippet-ready correction with AGD wording.
One table of every time limit (NOIM window, registration by the celebrant, certificate, CNI, apostille, overseas licences). Nobody has it.
Destination time limits for the countries Australian couples choose, in one place, linking to our country guides.
PAA on proof and registration ('What happens to a marriage that is not registered?', 'What is the best proof of marriage?') answered briefly and sourced.

outline.h2: Does a marriage licence expire in Australia?
outline.answers: The search itself, in the first 60 words.
must_include: Opening answer: Australia has no marriage licence; the Notice of Intended Marriage (NOIM) has a window (at least one month, no more than 18 months before the wedding), not a validity period; the official marriage certificate does not expire. Wording from pillar final.md lines 86 and 104 and research batch A.
Link up to the pillar in this section with a descriptive anchor.
Key takeaways block (3 to 5 specific sentences) right after the intro, including the 'what lasts how long' summary.

outline.h2: The NOIM window: what '18 months' really means
outline.answers: How long is a NOIM valid? The myth, the rule, and how 'one month' is counted.
must_include: Myth vs rule in two sentences; cite AGD and Marriage Act s 42 (batch A).
How the one month is counted (a calendar month, not 30 days) if batch A confirms.
Worked example with a date (e.g. wedding on a Saturday in October 2027: earliest and latest dates to give notice). Label as an example.
No how-to on lodging or witnessing: one sentence and the pillar link.

outline.h2: If your date moves: postponing, changing celebrant or venue
outline.answers: Does a NOIM 'lapse' if the wedding is postponed past 18 months, or if the celebrant changes?
must_include: What AGD says about a wedding that does not take place within 18 months of the notice, and whether a new NOIM is needed (batch A; if not stated officially, say 'ask your celebrant' and do not guess).
Changing celebrant: the NOIM can be transferred (pillar covers this briefly; batch A to confirm wording); one or two lines only.
Invisible work: when a date moves, the celebrant, venue, overseas documents and guest travel all have to be re-timed together. This is where an advisor earns their keep.

outline.h2: After the wedding: does a marriage certificate expire?
outline.answers: Certificate expiry, registration, proof of marriage.
must_include: The celebrant must send the paperwork to the state registry within a set time (batch A/B: exact deadline and wording).
The official registry certificate does not expire; the ceremonial certificate is not proof for most purposes (batch A/B wording).
Some overseas authorities, embassies or agencies ask for a recently issued copy; say this only as far as official sources support it (batch A/B).
PAA: 'What happens to a marriage that is not registered?' and 'What is the best proof of marriage?' answered in one or two sourced sentences each, or moved to FAQ.
Link /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate for marriages registered abroad, descriptive anchor.

outline.h2: Documents with a shelf life when you marry abroad
outline.answers: Which supporting papers lapse: CNI, apostilles, recently issued birth certificates, translations.
must_include: Certificate of No Impediment (DFAT): whether DFAT states a validity, and that destination countries often set their own (batch A).
Apostille (DFAT): the apostille itself does not carry an expiry from DFAT, but receiving countries may require recent documents; only if official sources say so (batch A).
'Issued within X months' rules belong to the destination country; point to the table in the next H2.
Practical line: order these documents last, close to travel, inside the destination's limit.

Links: Italy legal guide; Greece licence guide only if published; destination pages from link-map for the new rows.
Line: 'Rules change; confirm with the destination's authorities and the Australian embassy before booking.'

outline.h2: Putting the clocks together: a validity timeline for a destination wedding
outline.answers: When to request each document so nothing lapses before the day. Invisible-work section; answers fear A. Ends with the advisor role (fear B and paying parent).
must_include: Backward timeline labelled as an example: NOIM window (if marrying in Australia), CNI and apostilles ordered inside the destination's limit, overseas licence or banns window, travel, ceremony, registration, certificate.

The coordination nobody sees: aligning document dates with venue contracts, celebrant or officiant availability, guest arrivals and a wet-weather or rescheduling plan that does not push a document past its limit.
Where a Wedded Advisor helps (brand-profile framing only, no prices): mapping every clock to one calendar, re-timing documents when a date moves.
One line on /wedded-world (no ticket push).
Closing discovery_call CTA.

pick_three_more.why: One of the most popular destinations for Australian couples; link-map has /destinations/oceania/fiji. Fiji issues a marriage licence through its registry.
pick_three_more.research_ask: Official Fiji Births, Deaths and Marriages or Fiji Government source for how long the licence is valid and any 'issued within' rules for supporting documents. Drop if no official figure.

pick_three_more.why: Luxury favourite (Provence, Paris, chateaux); link-map has /destinations/europe/france.
pick_three_more.research_ask: service-public.fr or French embassy in Australia: validity of the publication of banns and the 'issued within X months' rule for birth certificates. Note residency requirement in one line only.

pick_three_more.why: Growing luxury destination (Douro, Sintra, Algarve); link-map has /destinations/europe/portugal.
pick_three_more.research_ask: IRN / justica.gov.pt or Portuguese embassy: validity of the preliminary marriage process (processo preliminar) and document age rules.

alternates_if_a_pick_fails.why: Very popular with Australians; state licence has a published validity on hawaii.gov.

Hugely popular, but legal marriage for foreigners is complex and many couples marry at home; include only if an official source states a time limit, otherwise mention in one line that most Australian couples marry legally at home and celebrate in Bali.
